newsitem.title: MEXICO: Eight henchmen of Mexican drug lord sentenced.
newsitem.headline: Eight henchmen of Mexican drug lord sentenced.

text.p: Eight gunmen from the Arellano Felix drug cartel were sentenced to varying prison sentences for their roles in one of the most feared criminal organisations in Mexico, a judge said on Wednesday.
The eight, whose sentences ranged from 33 months to 15 years, also are accused of participating in the 1993 murder of a Roman Catholic cardinal in a separate case.
"The sentences were dictated yesterday (Tuesday) against eight people for diverse federal offences," Judge Isidro Avelar Gutierrez of the western state of Jalisco told Reuters.
The eight were convicted on an array of charges including criminal association, drug possession and weapons possession.
The Tijuana-based Arellano Felix brothers, among the most wanted men in Mexico, control much of the illegal drug trade along Mexico's border with California.
The eight men were arrested in September 1994, accused of participating in the 1993 assassination of Cardinal Juan Jesus Posadas Ocampo at the Guadalajara international airport.
The cardinal is widely considered to have been the victim of mistaken identity in an attempted hit on a rival drug lord.
But that crime was a state offence and will be taken up separately from the federal crimes for which the men were sentenced on Tuesday, the judge said.

The eight men also were accused of participating in a car-bomb explosion at a luxury hotel as well as the attempted murder of Amado Carrillo Fuentes, another powerful drug baron who controls the Juarez cartel.

The two longest prison terms were given to Samuel Niebla Rivera, also known as "El Ochapito," 15 years, and Jorge Isaias Mark Hernandez, eight years. The six others each received two years and nine months.
None will be granted bail "because they are accused of other grave offences ... most of them have a history of homicides," the judge said.
